title: Ratchet & Clank (USA, SCUS_971.99), every C unit compiled with the pinned ee-gcc 2.9-991111-01
setup: mkdir -p tools/compilers && ln -sfn {tool:ee-gcc2.9-991111-01} tools/compilers/sdk-compiler && ln -sfn compilers tools/cc

rm -rf {work}/game-compiler {work}/sn && mkdir -p {work}/game-compiler/include {work}/sn/bin {work}/sn/ee/bin && printf '#!/bin/sh
exec {tool:ee-gcc2.9-991111-01}/bin/ee-gcc "$@"
' > {work}/game-compiler/ee-gcc && printf '#!/bin/sh
exec {tool:binutils-mips-ps2-decompals}/mips-ps2-decompals-as "$@"
' > {work}/game-compiler/as && chmod +x {work}/game-compiler/ee-gcc {work}/game-compiler/as && ln -sf {tool:ee-gcc2.9-991111-01}/lib/gcc-lib/ee/2.9-ee-991111-01/cc1 {work}/game-compiler/cc1 && ln -sf {tool:ee-gcc2.95.3-114}/bin/ee-gcc.exe {work}/sn/bin/ee-gcc.exe && ln -sf {tool:ee-gcc2.95.3-114}/lib/gcc-lib/ee/2.95.3/ps2eeas.exe {work}/sn/ee/bin/Ps2EeAs.exe
limits: Ratchet & Clank (Lombyte) builds its SDK block with the vendored ee-gcc 2.9-991111-01 (= the pinned `ee-gcc2.9-991111-01`) but its game code with a reconstructed Sony/Cygnus 2.9-ee-991111b built from a GPL source archive and a patch stack (`scripts/build-game-compiler.py`: needs a 32-bit host toolchain, `gcc -m32`) and assembled by Ps2EeAs 1.9.25.758 under wine. Neither is in toolchains.json and the lane host has no 32-bit development files and no root. The lane therefore takes the commands of the repo's own source-only objdiff base build (`build/src/**/*.c.o`: `ee-gcc -c -O2 -g2 -gstabs` with the SDK compiler for every unit, game units included) and compiles every unit with the pinned 2.9-991111-01. SDK units are compiled as the repo compiles them; a game unit matches only where the SDK compiler and the game compiler agree, so the matched count is far below the repo's own and is dominated by the SDK block. `configure.py` insists on a game compiler, so `tools/compilers/game-compiler` is a stub (the pinned driver) that no unit of this lane uses.

The oracle objects the repo's `link` build uses for units without a matching compile are copies of retail bytes; they are not compiled from C and are excluded (units whose compile source is not a `.c` file are skipped).
